service_boundary: Represents Databricks-hosted Foundation Model APIs and serving endpoints, not external-model credentials merely governed through Unity AI Gateway, MLflow alone, or model publishers' direct APIs.
regional_controls: Databricks documents region-specific model availability and treats Foundation Model APIs as a Designated Service using Databricks Geos for processing residency.
retention_controls: Logging and data processing follow workspace, serving-endpoint, and Databricks Geo controls; externally hosted models remain a separate downstream data boundary.
routing: Unity AI Gateway can apply governance across hosted and external model endpoints; this record's managed-host boundary covers Databricks-served models and endpoints.
customization: Provisioned throughput supports fine-tuned variants, supported architectures, and customer model weights registered through Unity Catalog.
strengths: Inference integrates with Unity Catalog governance and Databricks data workflows.
Pay-per-token, priority, provisioned, and batch modes cover distinct workloads.
tradeoffs: Capabilities and model catalogs differ across AWS, Azure, GCP, and regions.
External model routing can add separate provider terms beyond the hosted-service boundary.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference or the security documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Databricks Foundation Model APIs documentation, for Databricks Foundation Model APIs

upstream_disclosure.note: Scoped to the external-models feature. The documentation states: "External models are third-party models hosted outside of Databricks." Whether Databricks-hosted proprietary models (its own GPT, Claude, and Gemini offerings) route content to the underlying model's own infrastructure is not stated.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Databricks external-models documentation, for Databricks Foundation Model APIs

credential_handling.note: The model-serving documentation states: "You must store credentials like your API key or other tokens as a Databricks secret." Databricks secrets are held in an encrypted store.
credential_handling.scope: Databricks model-serving secrets documentation, for Databricks Foundation Model APIs

cache_isolation.note: The operator's own engineering blog states: "Security is a first-class concern at Databricks. Prompt caches are isolated, only reside in volatile memory and are never persisted."
cache_isolation.scope: Databricks prompt-caching engineering blog post, for Databricks Foundation Model APIs

vulnerability_disclosure.note: A security.txt file is published: "Policy: https://www.databricks.com/trust", "Contact: security@databricks.com", "Bug Bounty: https://hackerone.com/databricks".
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Databricks security.txt, for Databricks Foundation Model APIs

independent_audit.note: The Databricks compliance page states SOC reports are available on request and does not name Foundation Model APIs specifically.
independent_audit.scope: Databricks SOC compliance page, read for Databricks Foundation Model APIs
